extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection in 404 Error Handler — Remote code execution on the server, full compromise of the application. [verified: request.url is interpolated via .format() into a Jinja2 template string, then render_template_string processes it without any sanitization or escaping of template syntax, allowing SSTI and remote code execution.]

Insecure Pickle Deserialization — Remote code execution on the server. [verified: The /about/sync endpoint accepts attacker-controlled hex-encoded input from 'data_obj', writes it to a file, and deserializes it with pickle.load() without any validation or sanitization, enabling arbitrary code execution.]

Insecure YAML Deserialization — Remote code execution on the server. [verified: No input validation or safe loader is used; base64-decoded user input is passed directly to yaml.load() on line 18, enabling arbitrary code execution via malicious YAML payloads.]

SQL Injection in Dashboard.getPage — Attacker can extract all data from the SQLite database, including user credentials, bypass authentication, modify data. [verified: The pageId parameter from the /dashboard/<pageId> route is passed directly into the SQL query string without parameterization or sanitization, as shown in Dashboard.py line 7. No input validation or escaping is applied, allowing an attacker to craft a malicious pageId to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the SQLite database.]

SQL Injection in Dashboard Page Retrieval — Unauthorized reading, modification, or deletion of database contents, including user credentials and messages. [verified: The `pageId` URL parameter is passed directly to `Dashboard().getPage(pageId)` with no input validation or sanitization, and the check `if pageId == 0` does not provide security because `pageId` is a string. No compensating control is present.]

Path Traversal in XML_download — Unauthorized read of any file on the filesystem, including application source, database, secrets. [verified: The /validator/getXML endpoint takes user input from request.form['example_file'] and passes it directly to open() without any path validation or sanitization, enabling arbitrary file reads via path traversal sequences.]

Path Traversal in XML_upload (Arbitrary File Write) — Arbitrary file write, potentially leading to code execution by overwriting templates or other files (limited by extension check). [verified: The XML_upload endpoint at /validator/uploads saves the uploaded file using file.save('uploads/'+filename) where filename is directly taken from the user-controlled file.filename with only an extension check (allowed_file).
